opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next generations of CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators — up 8% year over year as AMD invested more in AI.

opex.name: Marketing, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Writing down the value of technology bought in acquisitions (Xilinx above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash — shown net of a $13M licensing gain.

footerNote: Cost of sales of $2,913M includes $230M of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, on top of $2,683M of cost of sales before that amortization, following AMD's own presentation of its income statement. The amortization line in operating expenses is shown as $379M — AMD's $392M of amortization net of a $13M licensing gain. The tax line was a $52M benefit, drawn as a green source into net profit.
oneTimers: Inventory loss of $65M at a third-party contract manufacturer, related to an incident at that manufacturer's facility — included in GAAP cost of sales and added back in AMD's non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Other income, net of $53M (primarily interest income from short-term investments, partly offset by losses on equity investments and foreign currency effects), plus $7M of equity income from an investee, less $25M of interest expense — a net +$35M. AMD reports equity income on its own line below the tax line; following the sibling AMD pages it is folded into otherIncomeM here and disclosed in this breakdown.

segments.name: Data Center
segments.note: EPYC server processors and Instinct AI accelerators — revenue hit a record $2.3B, up 80%, driven by the ramp of Instinct MI300 GPU shipments and growth in 4th Gen EPYC CPU sales.

segments.name: Client
segments.note: Ryzen processors for PCs — up 85%, driven primarily by Ryzen 8000 Series processor sales.

segments.name: Gaming
segments.note: Graphics cards and console chips — down 48% due to a decrease in semi-custom revenue and lower Radeon GPU sales.

segments.name: Embedded
segments.note: Chips built into industrial, communications and other equipment (the Xilinx business) — down 46% as customers continued to manage their inventory levels.

takeaways.text: Data Center revenue reached a record $2,337M, up 80% year over year on the ramp of Instinct MI300 AI accelerators and 4th Gen EPYC sales, and Client rose 85% to $1,368M on Ryzen 8000 sales — the two AI-and-PC businesses now bring in more than two-thirds of AMD's revenue.
takeaways.title: Data Center hit a record

takeaways.text: Operating income was just $36M — a 1% margin — because GAAP results carry $622M of acquisition-related amortization and $371M of stock-based compensation. On AMD's non-GAAP view, which strips those out, operating income was $1,133M. Net income of $123M also leaned on a $52M tax benefit.
takeaways.title: GAAP operating profit was barely positive

takeaways.text: Gaming revenue fell 48% to $922M on lower semi-custom console and Radeon sales, and Embedded fell 46% to $846M as customers worked through inventories — together wiping out almost all of the growth from Data Center and Client, so total revenue rose only 2% to $5,473M.
takeaways.title: Gaming and Embedded dragged total growth to 2%

verdict: AMD's revenue grew just 2% to $5.5B because record Data Center sales and a surging Client business were almost entirely offset by steep falls in Gaming and Embedded, leaving GAAP operating income at just $36M.
